thought.text: The log shows earlier successes (`GET / 200`, `GET /energie 200`) but my recent requests all returned 500. Let me retest and investigate what changed.

reasoning_content:
According to the tail of the log, the earlier checks (/ → 200, /energie → 200) succeeded, but the most recent requests are all returning 500. That's weird. In the final lines, / and /energie are returning 500 in about 40-50ms. Maybe the state of the dev server is broken — a previous compile error could be persisting. In the Next dev environment, even after a module-not-found error on a certain route, other routes should normally keep working.

Wait — actually, maybe the dev server is in a state where a compile failure has invalidated the whole tree. Let me re-request with a longer timeout and check. Or, the server might have crashed, and something else is responding. Let me check the logs a bit more and test once more.

Let me look at the entire log and test again. Also, let me check whether the dev server process is still alive (it was alive: the next-server v15.5.28 process).

The last lines "GET / 500 in 53ms" etc. were probably my curl just now. So even / is now returning 500. But the earlier GET / was 200 in 10420ms. What changed? Maybe the compilation of the broken routes has left the webpack cache in a broken state, or the dev server's filesystem watcher detected something. Or maybe the server is running out of memory (2.6GB of RAM). Let me check the system memory and retest.

action.command: sleep 5; for p in / /energie; do code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 180 "http://localhost:3000$p"); echo "$p -> $code"; done; echo "==="; free -m | head -3; echo "==="; tail -5 /tmp/dev-server-final.log
